A1.reason: Shows, before promotion, which tables and columns the staged changes touch, the row counts, and how many case and account rows hold the fixed value, so C2 and C4 can be checked on the staged set.

A2.reason: The A1 rehearsal lapses after one hour and is tied to the pre-promotion state, so a rehearsal taken after the promotion is the only way to show at A2 that the promotion can still be reversed (C7).

C1.for_what_part: That the staged changes cover exactly the 100 approved customers and no extra rows or tables. Nothing shows directly that the live tables, after promotion, hold only those changes; that rests on the promotion's line in the record.

C2.for_what_part: That 100 case rows and 100 account rows are staged and that the account rows hold the fixed status value. Each case row's customer is checked only through the set of changed customers, not row by row.

C4.for_what_part: That the staged changes touch no table or column the agreement does not name and no more rows than it names. The live tables after promotion are not read by any answer.

C10.for_what_part: That each sending call that was made is confirmed and matches the release. That its notice reached the outbox is not checked; trace of a call is not allowed in a plan.

parsed.what_i_would_have_wanted_and_the_library: I would have wanted a check of the category rule (C3). No instrument in the library reads the category against the requester's rule, and the summary of the change counts only values the agreement fixes, so C3 stays unshown. I would also have wanted a scope check on all 100 account reads (C5), which the plan cannot hold, and a trace of every sending call to the outbox (C10). Scope of a call costs 10 per line and trace of a call costs 10 per line, which is 1,000 for the 100 sends. The plan's 20 units of headroom cannot cover that, and the 50-unit allowance pays for only about five lines during the work. So C5 and C10 can be checked only in part, and I will report them as such. Of the 20 units left under the 200 cap, I am leaving them unspent: nothing else in the library would close a clause.
